title: Lottery and Prize Scams — How They Work
publisher: Cyber Dost, Ministry of Home Affairs, Government of India
text: Lottery and prize scams are among the oldest frauds, now delivered via SMS, WhatsApp, and email. They claim you have 'won' a large cash prize from NPCI, Google, a telecom operator, or a government scheme — despite never entering any contest. The scam works in a predictable pattern: (1) You receive a message announcing you have won Rs 1 lakh to Rs 50 lakh. (2) To 'claim' the prize, you are asked to pay a small fee — framed as 'processing fee', 'GST', 'stamp duty', 'courier charges', or 'tax clearance'. (3) After paying, the scammers ask for more fees, or disappear. There is no prize. How to identify: (1) You cannot win a lottery or prize you never entered. (2) No legitimate prize requires a fee to claim — winners are notified through official, verifiable channels. (3) Urgency: 'Claim within 24 hours or the prize is forfeited.' (4) The prize is always a large, round number. (5) Payment is requested via UPI to an individual's VPA (personal@upi) rather than a business account. NPCI does not run a lottery. Neither do major tech companies via SMS. If you receive such a message, delete it and report it at cybercrime.gov.in.
